The test image shows a corn stalk that has been pulled apart/broken, revealing:
- Dark brown/black rotted tissue around the outer ring of the break
- Soft, yellowish-cream decaying pith interior
- White stringy/slimy strands in the center (bacterial ooze)
- Wet, water-soaked appearance characteristic of bacterial infection

The reference collage for Bacterial_stalk_rot confirms this — the upper-left panel shows nearly identical features: a stalk cross-section with dark rotted edges, soft pith, and visible bacterial slime strands. The wet, slimy, dark-rimmed breakdown with no dry/powdery fungal elements rules out Charcoal, Diplodia, or Fusarium stalk rots.
